question.prompt: Handy Aaron helped a neighbor \(1 \frac{1}{4}\) hours on Monday, \(50\) minutes on Tuesday, from \(8:20\) to \(10:45\) on Wednesday morning, and a half-hour on Friday. He is paid \(\$3\) per hour. How much did he earn for the week?

solutions.explanation:
Put all the work times in minutes so they can be added. There are \(60\) minutes in an hour, so Monday's \(1\frac14\) hours is \(60+60\div4=75\) minutes. Friday's half-hour is \(30\) minutes.

On Wednesday, \(8{:}20\) to \(10{:}20\) is two hours, followed by another \(25\) minutes to \(10{:}45\). Thus Wednesday's work lasted \(2\times60+25=145\) minutes.

The week's total is
\[
75+50+145+30=300\text{ minutes}.
\]
Since \(300\div60=5\), Aaron worked \(5\) hours. At \(\$3\) per hour, he earned \(5\times\$3=\$15\), choice E.
solutions.title: Convert all work times to minutes
